title: The Man Waiting
summary: At a relay settlement used as neutral ground by travelers and locals, Ray Silvestro is already waiting for Kael under yet another identity: the Architect. Eva and Jessa now recognize the setup before Kael even answers.

panelPlan.text: Wide public room beneath the old relay tower: message boards, meal tables, travelers sleeping against walls, no sense of military control. Ray is conspicuously elegant among the dust.
Kael enters with Eva and Jessa. Ray stands from a table laid for two, as if an appointment has begun exactly on time.
Eva and Jessa exchange a look before Ray speaks. Kael notices their look before he looks at Ray.

directionInline.text: Ray is fancy, controlled and distinct from Kael. The repetition is now expected by the trio, which changes the dramatic energy from confusion to wary recognition.

title: The Appointment
summary: Ray says he was promised that the Architect would arrive today and settle an old betrayal. Eva presses on the promise rather than Kael's identity, while Kael tries to keep Ray from turning expectation into violence.

panelPlan.text: Ray sits opposite Kael at the prepared table. A sealed letter and an old brass token sit between them.
Eva stands nearby, asking who arranged the meeting. Ray dislikes being questioned by someone he did not plan for.
Ray opens the letter enough to show a description of Kael's coat, hair and mannerisms. The handwriting is not his.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: The preacher said you'd come today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: What did he say I was coming to do?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Same hands. Same way of watching the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did Samuel tell you that too?

directionInline.text: The trio now investigates the social setup in real time. The issue's tension comes from whether knowing the trick helps them escape it.

title: Samuel
summary: Eva finds Samuel not hiding but tending to a frightened family in a side room after a separate local dispute. He is exactly the preacher Isabelle described, and his genuine pastoral care makes him harder to reduce to a con man.

panelPlan.text: Eva follows a familiar sun-faded coat into a crowded side room. Samuel is bandaging a boy's hand while calming two adults who are arguing over blame.
Jessa arrives behind Eva and recognizes from her expression that the search is over. Samuel notices them but finishes tying the bandage before acknowledging them.
Eva puts Isabelle's name into the room. Samuel's face changes by less than Eva hoped, but enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Hold still. You're going to make me tie it twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's why I'm hurrying badly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Give me until the bandage is done.

directionInline.text: Samuel's care is real. He is morally compromised because he can manipulate people precisely because he actually listens to them.

title: The Setup Man
summary: Pressed by Eva and Jessa, Samuel admits that Veyra selected real unresolved identities from communities along Kael's route and sent him ahead to plant the expectation that Kael might be that person. Varnok and Saye were deliberate tests. Merrit was different: the resemblance story existed before Samuel reached the Mirage, and he only amplified it by predicting Merrit's return.

panelPlan.text: Outside the side room, Eva blocks Samuel's path while Jessa leans against the opposite wall, giving him only one comfortable direction to look.

Samuel produces practical route notes: existing people and grievances tied to Varnok, Saye, Merrit and the Architect, with marks showing where he primed an expectation and where a story predated him. These are case notes, not invented aliases or mystical evidence.
Eva realizes the conspiracy is mundane enough to be worse: somebody has been deliberately using entire communities to test Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: But you told people Kael was coming.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I told them a man matching him might be.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You told Isabelle he was coming.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: After Veyra heard the Merrit story. I pushed it. I didn't start it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Because Veyra thought one of those men was Kael, and I was good at making people talk.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You were good at making them hurt.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Did they know they were helping you?

directionInline.text: Causal rule: Veyra and Samuel do not invent fake biographies as random traps. They exploit real unresolved identities and prime communities to map Kael onto them, then watch whether Kael reveals knowledge. Merrit is the first candidate whose association with Kael was not initiated by their priming.

title: Veyra's Question
summary: Veyra arrives after Ray's confrontation has cooled and admits she has been following Kael's contradictory story. She believed one identity must be real and began engineering encounters to make him reveal which one.

panelPlan.text: Veyra enters the public room from the opposite door as Samuel, Eva and Jessa return. Kael sees her and understands immediately that she is the she.
Ray remains nearby, angry to learn his grievance was used as leverage. Veyra does not apologize by calling it necessary; she states what she did and why.
Kael asks the simplest question: did it work? Veyra looks at the four names on Samuel's list and cannot honestly say yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I thought one name would catch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Something you knew. A place. A person. A lie you had rehearsed badly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I assumed I had the wrong bait.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: No. It's all I can say without pretending it was better than it was.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Did it tell you anything about me?

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I believe the other answers failed.

directionInline.text: Veyra is a pursuer with a human theory, not an omniscient scientist. Her methods are controlled; her certainty is not.

title: The One She Didn't Plant
summary: The first arc ends with a precise distinction. Veyra and Samuel explain how they amplified Varnok, Saye and the Architect, but Merrit was already an independent resemblance story before Samuel primed Isabelle. Their conspiracy explains several appointments, not the existence of every candidate identity.

panelPlan.text: The group stands in the relay settlement's public room after the confrontation. The social danger has passed, but nobody feels relieved.

Eva works through Samuel's route notes in order. Varnok, Saye and Architect carry Samuel's marks; Merrit points back to an earlier report from a traveler out of the Mirage and Isabelle's preexisting damaged photograph.

Outside, Kael walks toward the rig. Jessa follows. Eva lingers just long enough to hear Veyra's answer, then runs after them. A distant Sunforge shape catches late light beyond the settlement; nobody looks at it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I made Isabelle expect him. I didn't give her the man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So somebody else put Kael's face in that story first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: That wasn't the part I regretted.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You still think this is people seeing what they want?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I think that happens a lot.

directionInline.text: Worldview reset #1: Veyra and Samuel can account for the primed expectation and timing of several encounters, but Merrit's resemblance to Kael entered Veyra's investigation from outside their own operation. The human conspiracy is real and causally limited.
